column1: # CLAIMS.tsv -- every number this README states, and the command that printed it.
# Read tools/claimcheck.py's header for why this file exists. The short version:
# this README once said twoprinters was 73/73 while the script printed 66/67, and
# said 77/77 beside single-all.sh which prints 78/78. Nothing caught either,
# because no gate read the prose. This file is what a gate reads.
#   python3 tools/claimcheck.py --all      # also single-all / twoprinters / e2e-all
#   python3 tools/claimcheck.py --sweep    # numbers in README.md with no row here
# Columns:  FILE <TAB> ANCHOR <TAB> CLASS <TAB> NUMBER <TAB> SOURCE <TAB> EXTRACT <TAB> GUARD
# The cheap rows are deliberately the DENOMINATORS. A numerator needs the whole
# gate; a denominator is `ls`. Both of this repo's real defects were denominator
# drift -- the corpus grew from 77 to 78 and the prose did not follow -- so the
# rows that cost a second are the ones that would have caught them.

column5: bash -c 'n=$(ls examples/*.nim | wc -l); m=$(for d in examples/*/; do [ -f "$d/main.nim" ] && echo x; done | wc -l); echo "corpus=$((n+m))"'
